html:
Botswana is a landlocked country in southern Africa, mostly covered by the Kalahari Desert. It was the British Bechuanaland Protectorate from 1885 and became independent in 1966.

Its main people, the Batswana, are Bantu speakers who settled the area well over a thousand years ago, next to older San foragers. In the 1800s Tswana chiefdoms faced Boer settlers from the east. Britain declared a protectorate in 1885, mainly to keep the road north open for its own expansion.

In 1895 three chiefs, among them Khama III, travelled to London to stop Britain handing their land to Cecil Rhodes and his British South Africa Company. They largely succeeded. Britain spent little on the protectorate and ran it from Mafeking, a town outside its borders.

  • 1948: the heir to the Bamangwato throne, Seretse Khama, married a white Englishwoman. Pressure from South Africa led Britain to exile him.
  • 1966: independence, with Seretse Khama as first president.
  • 1967: diamonds were found. The Orapa mine opened in 1971, run jointly with De Beers.

Diamond money, spent on roads, schools and clinics, took Botswana from one of the poorest countries in the world to a middle-income one. It has held elections without a break since independence, and the ruling party lost power peacefully in 2024. Its worst blow was the AIDS epidemic, which hit it among the hardest of any country.
sum: Botswana is a landlocked country in southern Africa, mostly covered by the Kalahari Desert. It was the British Bechuanaland Protectorate from 1885 and became independent in 1966.
